docs.title: 🎮 Create Your Own Catching Game!
docs.text:
Welcome to the Scratch Catching Game course! In this guide, you will learn how to build your very own game where you control a character and catch falling objects.

What you will create: A fun game where you move left and right to catch good items for points, avoid the bad items, and win the game!

docs.title: What is Scratch?
docs.text: Scratch is a fun way to learn coding! Instead of typing hard words, you snap colorful blocks together like LEGO. It is the perfect place to create your own games, stories, and animations.

docs.title: What you need:
docs.text:
• A computer with internet access
  • Your Scratch account (go to scratch.mit.edu to log in)
  • A big imagination! 🧠✨

docs.title: How to use this guide:
docs.text: Read each module step-by-step. Don't rush! Make sure to test your game often. If you see a challenge, try it out!

docs.title: 🛑 Listen to Teacher First!
docs.text: Wait! Before you begin: Your teacher is going to show you the basics on the screen. Please watch and listen carefully! Once the teacher says "Go!", you can come back to this guide and start making your game.

docs.title: 🎉 Congratulations!
docs.text: You did it! You have built a complete, working video game in Scratch. You learned how to use coordinates, loops, variables, and conditions. You are a real coder now!

docs.title: Next Challenges
docs.text:
Do you want to keep going? Try adding these cool features to your game: - ⏱️ Timer Mode: Can you add a timer that counts down from 30 seconds? Try to get the highest score before time runs out! - 🛒 Shop Upgrade Mode: Use points to buy a faster character! - 👾 Boss Battle Mode: When you reach 20 points, a big boss appears! - 👯 Two Player Mode: Add a second player who uses the A and D keys to move. Who can catch the most?

Keep creating and have fun! 🚀

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text:
• What the Scratch screen looks like
  • What a Sprite is
  • How to find coding blocks
  • How to change the Backdrop (background)

docs.title: Step-by-Step Instructions
docs.text:
1. Open a new project in Scratch.
  2. Look at the left side: This is where all your Blocks are.
  3. Look at the middle: This is your Code Area where you drag blocks to build your script.
  4. Look at the top right: This is the Stage where your game happens.
  5. Look at the bottom right: This is the Sprite Area. A Sprite is your game character or object!

docs.title: Add Image Here
docs.text: [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show Scratch interface with arrows pointing to Blocks, Code Area, Stage, and Sprite Area]

docs.title: Try It Yourself
docs.text: Drag one blue move 10 steps block into the middle. Click it and see what happens to the cat!

docs.title: Challenge Yourself
docs.text: Can you find the button to delete the cat sprite? (Hint: look for a little trash can!)

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
• [ ] I know where the coding blocks are.
  • [ ] I know where the Stage is.
  • [ ] I know what a Sprite is.

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text:
• How to add controls for your player
  • How to make your player move left and right

docs.title: Step-by-Step Instructions
docs.text:
1. Pick a Sprite to be your player.
  2. Go to Events (yellow) and drag out when [right arrow] key pressed.
  3. Go to Motion (blue) and drag change x by 10. Attach it under the event block.
  4. Go to Events again and drag out when [left arrow] key pressed.
  5. Go to Motion and drag change x by -10. Attach it under the event block.

docs.title: Add Image Here
docs.text: [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show Scratch blocks for right and left movement]

docs.title: Try It Yourself
docs.text: Press the left and right arrow keys on your keyboard. Does your player move?

docs.title: Challenge Yourself
docs.text: Change the number from 10 to 20. What happens to your player when you press the keys now?

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
• [ ] My player moves right.
  • [ ] My player moves left.

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text:
• How to change the Backdrop
  • How to choose a player Sprite that fits your game world

docs.title: Step-by-Step Instructions
docs.text:
1. Look at the bottom right corner of the screen and click the Choose a Backdrop button (it looks like a little picture).
  2. Pick a background for your game. (Is it a forest? Space? The ocean?)
  3. Click the Choose a Sprite button (it looks like a cat face) to add a new player Sprite.
  4. Delete any Sprites you don't need anymore.

docs.title: Add Image Here
docs.text: [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show the "Choose a Backdrop" and "Choose a Sprite" buttons]

docs.title: Try It Yourself
docs.text: Move your new player Sprite to the bottom of the screen. This is where they will catch things!

docs.title: Challenge Yourself
docs.text: Can you find a Backdrop and a Sprite that belong together? (Example: A fish in the ocean, or an astronaut in space!)

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
• [ ] I have chosen a Backdrop.
  • [ ] I have a player Sprite that fits my theme.

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text:
• How to add an object to catch
  • How to make it fall from the top of the screen
  • How to make it reset when it hits the bottom

docs.title: Step-by-Step Instructions
docs.text:
1. Add a new Sprite. This will be the object you want to catch!
  2. Add a when green flag clicked block (Events).
  3. Under it, add a forever loop (Control - orange).
  4. Inside the loop, put a change y by -5 block (Motion). This makes it fall!
  5. Now, drag an if <> then block (Control) inside the forever loop.
  6. Put a touching [edge]? block (Sensing - light blue) inside the if block.
  7. If touching the edge, make the object go back up using go to x: [pick random -200 to 200] y: 150 (Motion & Operators - green).

docs.title: Add Image Here
docs.text: [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show the code blocks for the falling object, including the forever loop and the reset if touching the edge]

docs.title: Try It Yourself
docs.text: Click the Green Flag. Does your object fall down and then appear at the top again?

docs.title: Challenge Yourself
docs.text: Make the object fall faster by changing -5 to -10.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
• [ ] My object falls down continuously.
  • [ ] My object teleports back to the top when it hits the bottom.

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text: • How to know if your player catches the object

docs.title: Step-by-Step Instructions
docs.text:
1. Go to the code for your falling object.
  2. Add another if <> then block inside the forever loop.
  3. Put a touching [Player Sprite Name]? block (Sensing) inside the new if.
  4. If it touches the player, it should teleport back up! Use the same block as before: go to x: [pick random -200 to 200] y: 150.

docs.title: Add Image Here
docs.text: [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show the blocks that check if the falling object is touching the player, and then resets its position]

docs.title: Try It Yourself
docs.text: Play your game! Try to catch the object. Does it disappear and go back to the top when you touch it?

docs.title: Challenge Yourself
docs.text: Can you add a fun sound effect when the player catches the object? Look in the Sound tab!

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text: • [ ] The object resets to the top when my player touches it.

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text:
• What a variable is
  • How to create a Score
  • How to add points when you catch an object

docs.title: Step-by-Step Instructions
docs.text:
1. Go to the Variables category (dark orange).
  2. Click Make a Variable and name it Score.
  3. Go to your Backdrop's code (or Player code) and add: when green flag clicked -> set [Score] to 0.
  4. Go back to your falling object's code. Find the if touching [Player] block.
  5. Inside that if, add change [Score] by 1.

docs.title: Add Image Here
docs.text: [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show the "Make a Variable" button and the blocks to set score to 0 and change score by 1]

docs.title: Try It Yourself
docs.text: Play the game and catch the object. Does your Score go up? When you click the Green Flag again, does the Score go back to zero?

docs.title: Challenge Yourself
docs.text: Give yourself 5 points for every catch instead of 1 point!

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
• [ ] My score goes up when I catch the object.
  • [ ] My score resets to 0 when I restart the game.

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text:
• How to set a score target
  • How to show a "You Win" message

docs.title: Step-by-Step Instructions
docs.text:
1. Go to your Backdrop's code.
  2. Add a new when green flag clicked block.
  3. Add a forever loop.
  4. Inside, add an if <> then block.
  5. For the condition, use the green Operator [ ] > [ ]. Put Score in the left box and 10 in the right box.
  6. If Score > 10, add a block to say [You Win!] for 2 seconds (Looks - purple), and then stop all (Control).

docs.title: Add Image Here
docs.text: [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show the blocks that check if score > 10 and display the win message]

docs.title: Try It Yourself
docs.text: Play until you get more than 10 points. Does the game stop and tell you that you won?

docs.title: Challenge Yourself
docs.text: Instead of making the sprite say "You Win!", can you change the Backdrop to a special WIN screen?

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
• [ ] The game stops when I reach my score target.
  • [ ] I see a "You Win!" message.

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text:
• How to find the Sound Library
  • How to add sound effects for catching, losing points, and winning

docs.title: Step-by-Step Instructions
docs.text:
1. Click on your player Sprite. Go to the Sounds tab at the top.
  2. Click the speaker icon to Choose a Sound (like "pop", "coin", or "magic spell").
  3. Go back to the Code tab.
  4. When you catch a good object, use the start sound [pop] block (Sound - pink).
  5. Add a bad sound (like "bonk") when you touch an enemy!
  6. Add a happy sound when you win.

docs.title: Add Image Here
docs.text: [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show the code with "start sound" blocks added for catching and hitting an enemy]

docs.title: Try It Yourself
docs.text: Play your game with the volume up!

docs.title: Challenge Yourself
docs.text: Can you add a background music track that loops forever?

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
• [ ] I hear a sound when I catch a good object.
  • [ ] I hear a different sound when I hit an enemy.

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text:
• How to make your game look polished
  • How to add a title screen

docs.title: Step-by-Step Instructions
docs.text:
1. Paint a new Sprite and use the Text tool to type your game's name. (This is your Title Screen!)
  2. Add code to your Title Sprite: when green flag clicked, show, go to x:0 y:0.
  3. Add a block to hide it after a few seconds: wait 3 seconds, then hide.

docs.title: Add Image Here
docs.text: [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show the blocks for the Title Screen sprite (show, wait 3 seconds, hide)]

docs.title: Try It Yourself
docs.text: Start the game. Does your title screen appear and then vanish so you can play?

docs.title: Challenge Yourself
docs.text: Can you use the Paint tool to draw your own custom Sprite or Backdrop?

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
• [ ] My game has a title screen that appears at the start.
  • [ ] My sprites and backgrounds look exactly how I want them.

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text:
• How to test your game like a real game developer
  • How to fix bugs

docs.title: Step-by-Step Instructions
docs.text:
1. Swap seats with a partner.
  2. Let them play your game without you telling them how.
  3. Watch them play. Is it too hard? Too easy? Is anything broken?
  4. Write down one thing you can fix or improve.
  5. Go back to your computer and make that improvement!

docs.title: Add Image Here
docs.text: [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show a fun image of characters playing a game together or testing]

docs.title: Try It Yourself
docs.text: What did your partner think of the game? Did they find any bugs?

docs.title: Challenge Yourself
docs.text: Fix a bug your partner found before the showcase!

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
• [ ] I watched someone else play my game.
  • [ ] I made at least one improvement based on testing.

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text: • How to present your work to others

docs.title: Step-by-Step Instructions
docs.text:
1. Get ready to show the class your game!
  2. Be prepared to share:
  3. Your game's name
  4. How to play (the controls)
  5. The coolest feature or your favorite part

docs.title: Add Image Here
docs.text: [PLACE IMAGE HERE – example of a completed Scratch project page]

docs.title: Try It Yourself
docs.text: Practice what you will say with your partner first.

docs.title: Challenge Yourself
docs.text: Add instructions in the "Instructions" box on your Scratch project page so anyone online knows how to play.

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text: • [ ] I am ready to share my game!

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text:
• How to create objects you should avoid (like a bomb, ghost, or rock!)
  • How to lose points

docs.title: Step-by-Step Instructions
docs.text:
1. Add a new Sprite to be your enemy object.
  2. Copy the falling code from your good object to your bad object. (Hint: You can click and drag the code from one sprite to another!)
  3. In the enemy's code, change the catch detection: when touching [Player], make it change [Score] by -1 (lose points!).
  4. Make sure the enemy also teleports back to the top after you touch it!

docs.title: Add Image Here
docs.text: [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show the enemy code blocks where score is changed by -1]

docs.title: Try It Yourself
docs.text: Test your game. What happens to your score when you hit the enemy?

docs.title: Challenge Yourself
docs.text: Can you make the game end ("Game Over") if your score goes below zero?

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
• [ ] I have an enemy object falling.
  • [ ] My score goes down when I touch the enemy.

docs.title: What You Will Learn
docs.text:
• How to make the game harder and more fun
  • How to change falling speeds

docs.title: Step-by-Step Instructions
docs.text:
1. Make your enemy fall faster! Change its falling speed to change y by -8.
  2. Add more good objects by right-clicking your good object Sprite and selecting duplicate.
  3. Make sure the duplicated objects fall from different starting spots at the top!

docs.title: Add Image Here
docs.text: [PLACE IMAGE HERE – show how to right-click and duplicate a sprite]

docs.title: Try It Yourself
docs.text: Play your game with multiple good objects and a fast enemy. Is it harder now?

docs.title: Challenge Yourself
docs.text: Can you add a super rare item that falls very fast but gives you 10 points?

docs.title: Checkpoint
docs.text:
• [ ] The enemy falls faster than the good objects.
  • [ ] I have more than one good object falling.
